Goal: Determine if pressure 4.5 atm can be achieved without exceeding temperature 120°C, using Gay-Lussac (P/T constant at constant V). Also compare 4.5 atm with 80% of max pressure achievable if gas compressed to half volume (3 m³) at same temperature.

Given: initial condition: T1 = 70°C, P1 = 4 atm, constant volume (V = 6 m³). Use ideal gas law: P/T (in Kelvin) constant.

Compute T2 for P2=4.5 atm: T2 = T1 * P2/P1. Convert T1 to K: 70°C = 343 K. So T2 = 343 * 4.5/4 = 343 * 1.125 = 386. (approx) 386.0 K = 113°C. That's ≤120°C, so feasible.

Now max pressure when volume halved (V2 = 3 m³) at same temperature (presumably same as initial? The statement: "ở cùng nhiệt độ" meaning same temperature as initial? It says "ở cùng nhiệt độ" after compressing to half volume. Likely same temperature as initial (70°C). Using Boyle's law (P1 V1 = P2 V2) at constant T. So P_max = P1 * V1/V2 = 4 atm * 6/3 = 8 atm. 80% of that = 0.8 * 8 = 6.4 atm. Compare 4.5 atm with 6.4 atm: 4.5 atm is less than 6.4 atm.
